description: HPO terms for the 20 gamt checklist items (configs/checklists/gamt.json), chosen on 2026-11-15 by a Claude helper from the pinned HPO release by name and synonym search and hierarchy checks (pipeline/extract/hpo_lookup.py), D-40 as extended by D-47. 'observed' is the one term a record may assert when the item is observed; null where the item is a composite no single term covers exactly (the free-text feature rows carry the specific term); for the basal ganglia MRI item the observed term is a broader ancestor, flagged in the note. 'excluded' lists every term a record may mark excluded when the item is explicitly absent. Flagged for review by Jimmy or the panel; not a pre-registered choice.

developmental delay or intellectual disa.note: Composite: Global developmental delay (EXACT 'Developmental delay') and Intellectual disability; neither is an ancestor of the other. Their nearest common ancestor (Neurodevelopmental abnormality) is broader, and Neurodevelopmental delay is not excluded because it also covers speech delay, which belongs to the speech item.

developmental regression.note: Developmental regression; exact name match (EXACT 'Loss of developmental milestones'); Motor regression and Cognitive regression are descendants.

absent or limited speech.note: Composite: Absent speech (EXACT 'Nonverbal') and Poor speech; neither is an ancestor of the other. Delayed speech and language development (parent of Absent speech) is not used: delay is not the same as limited speech, and its absence would overstate the exclusion. Their common ancestor Abnormal speech pattern is broader (dysarthria, stuttering).

seizures or epilepsy.note: Seizure (EXACT 'Seizures'; synonym 'Epilepsy'); the seizure types the item covers (myoclonic, tonic, absence, generalized, focal) are descendants.

abnormal eeg.note: EEG abnormality (EXACT 'Abnormal EEG'); slowing and epileptiform discharges are descendants.

chorea, choreoathetosis or ballismus.note: Composite: Chorea (Choreoathetosis is its descendant, so excluding Chorea covers it) and Hemiballismus (non-EXACT synonym 'Ballismus'; HPO has no separate ballismus term). Their common parent Involuntary movements is broader (tremor, myoclonus), so observed is null.

stereotypies (stereotypic hand movements.note: Motor stereotypy (EXACT 'Stereotypic behaviour', 'Repetitive movements'); Stereotypic upper-extremity movements (HP:5200018), for hand stereotypies, is a descendant.

autistic features (poor eye contact, imp.note: Composite: Autistic behavior (EXACT 'ASD'; Autism is a descendant), Reduced eye contact (EXACT 'Poor eye contact') and Reduced social responsiveness (EXACT 'Impaired social interaction'); none is an ancestor of another, so a record reporting only poor eye contact cannot assert Autistic behavior and observed is null. Abnormal social behavior and Abnormal communication are broader (disinhibition, language) and are not excluded.

hyperactivity.note: Hyperactivity; exact name match. Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder is a descendant.

aggressive behaviour.note: Aggressive behavior (EXACT 'Aggression'); spelling variant of the item.

self-injurious behaviour.note: Self-injurious behavior (EXACT 'Self-injurious behaviours'); head-banging and self-biting are descendants.

globus pallidus or basal ganglia lesions.note: HPO has no general basal ganglia lesion term; Abnormal basal ganglia morphology (EXACT 'Abnormality of the basal ganglia') is true of every pallidal or basal ganglia lesion, so it is the observed term, though broader than the item (it also covers large or small basal ganglia and dysgenesis); it is not excluded for that reason. Excluded: Abnormal globus pallidus morphology, Abnormal basal ganglia MRI signal intensity and Bilateral basal ganglia lesions, all descendants of it.

white matter or brainstem signal abnorma.note: Composite: Hyperintensity of cerebral white matter on MRI, Hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI and Abnormal brainstem MRI signal intensity; no single term covers white matter and brainstem signal. Abnormal cerebral white matter morphology and Abnormal brainstem white matter morphology are broader than signal change (corpus callosum, cerebellar peduncles) and are not used.

cerebral atrophy or ventriculomegaly.note: Composite: Cerebral atrophy and Ventriculomegaly; neither is an ancestor of the other and they sit under different parents, so observed is null.

hearing loss.note: Hearing impairment (synonym 'Hearing loss'; EXACT 'Deafness', 'Hypacusis'); mild and sensorineural hearing impairment are descendants.
